title: Meridian Complaints: working a complaint from inbox to final response letter
summary: Meridian Complaints is the tool the complaints team uses to log and work every customer complaint. A complaint handler picks a complaint from the Inbox, investigates it on the Complaint Detail screen and writes notes as they go. When the investigation is done the handler records a decision to uphold, partially uphold or reject the complaint, with a reason and a written summary. For an upheld or partially upheld complaint the handler works out the refund and interest on the Redress screen, with a team lead as second approver over £500. The handler then sends the final response letter from Letter Preview, and the team lead watches the team's workload and SLA position on the Dashboard.
actors: Finance (owner of the interest rate table)

screens.name: Complaints Inbox
screens.purpose: Lists every open complaint sorted by SLA remaining, so a handler can pick the next one to work.

screens.name: Complaint Detail
screens.purpose: Shows one complaint's customer details, its timeline of events and the handler's notes, and lets the handler add notes or change the category.

screens.name: Decision
screens.purpose: Records the outcome of the investigation (uphold, partially uphold or reject) with a reason and a written summary of findings.

screens.name: Redress
screens.purpose: Calculates the money owed to the customer (refund plus simple interest) for an upheld or partially upheld complaint and lets the handler approve it.

screens.name: Letter Preview
screens.purpose: Shows the final response letter with merge fields filled from the complaint, decision and redress, and lets the handler send it.

screens.name: Dashboard
screens.purpose: Gives the team lead a team view of open complaints, SLA breaches, uphold rate and complaints received by month, with an export to spreadsheet.

actions.description: Clicks a column header to sort the inbox by that column
Double-clicks a row (or presses the row's Open button) to open the complaint
Types in the Write a note box and presses Add note
Presses Change next to Category to correct the category
Picks Decision in the left navigation once the investigation is done
Picks an Outcome: Uphold, Partially uphold or Reject
Chooses a Reason from the dropdown and writes the Summary of findings
Presses Record decision (disabled for handlers below grade 2)
Enters Refund amount and Days out of pocket and presses Recalculate to fill the Calculation table
Presses Approve redress (over £500 this raises a task for the team lead as second approver)
Reads the letter through and presses Send letter
Presses Export to download the dashboard figures as a spreadsheet

journey.description: The handler lands on the Complaints Inbox, which lists the open complaints sorted by SLA remaining.
The handler double-clicks a row to open the complaint.
On Complaint Detail the handler reviews the customer details and timeline, investigates, and records what they did as notes.
If the category is wrong the handler changes it and adds a note saying why.
When the investigation is done the handler goes to Decision, picks an outcome and a reason, writes a summary of at least 50 words and presses Record decision.
If the complaint is upheld or partially upheld the handler goes to Redress, enters the refund amount and days out of pocket, checks the calculated interest and total, and presses Approve redress.
If the redress is over £500 the system raises a task for the team lead to give second approval.
The handler opens Letter Preview, checks the merged final response letter and presses Send letter, which goes to print or, if the customer asked for it, email.
The team lead reviews the Dashboard figures and chart and can export them as a spreadsheet.

requirements.statement: The Complaints Inbox lists every open complaint.
requirements.rationale: The frame shows one row per complaint with statuses New, Investigating, Awaiting customer, Decided and Referred, so "open" covers every status seen; what "open" excludes and whether the list is limited to the handler's team are open questions.
requirements.source_quote: You land on the Inbox, which is every open complaint sorted by how long we've got left on it.

requirements.statement: When the handler opens the Complaints Inbox, the system sorts the list by SLA remaining with the least time left at the top.
requirements.rationale: On the frame the SLA remaining column is sorted ascending: 1d 05h at the top, Breached rows above the rest.
requirements.source_quote: You land on the Inbox, which is every open complaint sorted by how long we've got left on it.

requirements.statement: Each row in the Complaints Inbox shows the reference, customer, received date, category, status, owner and SLA remaining of one complaint.
requirements.rationale: The Owner column was seen on the frame but not named by the expert. Reference format seen: CMP-YYYY-NNNNN. Status is shown as a coloured badge.
requirements.source_quote: Each row has the reference, the customer, when it came in, the category, the status and the SLA countdown.

requirements.statement: When the handler clicks a column header in the Complaints Inbox, the system sorts the list by that column.
requirements.source_quote: You click a column header to sort, and most people sort by the SLA column.

requirements.statement: The system shows SLA remaining for each open complaint as the days and hours left until 8 weeks after the received date.
requirements.rationale: The 8-week rule comes from the inbox footer "Final response due within 8 weeks of receipt" and the timeline entry "Final response due (8-week deadline)"; the expert says the clock is sometimes wrong, so the exact start point and day-count are unconfirmed (see the SLA question). Format seen: "1d 05h".
requirements.source_quote: Each row has the reference, the customer, when it came in, the category, the status and the SLA countdown.

requirements.statement: When the 8-week deadline for a complaint has passed, the system shows the word Breached in its SLA remaining column.
requirements.rationale: Seen on the frame: rows past the deadline show "Breached" instead of a countdown. The expert did not describe this value.
requirements.source_quote: Each row has the reference, the customer, when it came in, the category, the status and the SLA countdown.

requirements.statement: When a complaint becomes more than 8 weeks old, the system refers it to the Ombudsman without any user action.
requirements.rationale: What the referral sends, and to whom, was not described; see the Ombudsman question.
requirements.source_quote: Anything over eight weeks old goes to the Ombudsman automatically, you'll see the status flip to Referred on its own.

requirements.statement: When the system refers a complaint to the Ombudsman, it sets the complaint status to Referred.
requirements.rationale: A Referred status badge was seen in the inbox.
requirements.source_quote: Anything over eight weeks old goes to the Ombudsman automatically, you'll see the status flip to Referred on its own.

requirements.statement: When the handler double-clicks a row in the Complaints Inbox, the system opens the Complaint Detail for that complaint.
requirements.source_quote: You double-click a row to open it and you get the Complaint Detail.

requirements.statement: When the handler presses the Open button on a row in the Complaints Inbox, the system opens the Complaint Detail for that complaint.
requirements.rationale: An Open button was seen on each inbox row; the expert only described double-clicking.
requirements.source_quote: You double-click a row to open it and you get the Complaint Detail.

requirements.statement: The Complaint Detail shows the customer's name, policy, phone, email, address, received date with channel, category, status and owner.
requirements.rationale: Policy, received channel, status and owner were seen on the frame but not named by the expert. Policy shows number and product together (POL-766800 · Pet insurance).
requirements.source_quote: Top left is the customer and their contact details, and on the right is the timeline, every event in order: received, acknowledged, assigned, and so on.

requirements.statement: The Complaint Detail shows a timeline of every event on the complaint in date order.
requirements.rationale: Events seen on the frame: Complaint received; Acknowledgement sent; Assigned to a handler; Customer contacted; Evidence requested; Final response due (8-week deadline). Each event shows its date and a one-line detail.
requirements.source_quote: on the right is the timeline, every event in order: received, acknowledged, assigned, and so on.

requirements.statement: When the handler presses Add note, the system saves the text in the Write a note box as a new note on the complaint.
requirements.source_quote: You type in the box and press Add note, and it stamps your name and the date on it.

requirements.statement: The system stamps each saved note with the name of the handler who added it and the date it was added.
requirements.rationale: Notes seen on the frame show "Vibo Walridge · 01/07/2026" above the note text.
requirements.source_quote: You type in the box and press Add note, and it stamps your name and the date on it.

requirements.statement: The system keeps the text of a saved note unchanged: no user can edit it.
requirements.rationale: Placeholder in the Write a note box also reads "cannot be edited afterwards". Whether this applies to supervisors and administrators is an open question.
requirements.source_quote: Notes can't be edited or deleted once they're saved.

requirements.statement: The system keeps every saved note on the complaint: no user can delete it.
requirements.source_quote: Notes can't be edited or deleted once they're saved.

requirements.statement: The handler can change the category of a complaint from the Complaint Detail.
requirements.rationale: A Change button was seen next to Category. Categories seen in the inbox: Delayed claim, Renewal, Mis-sold cover, Policy wording, Poor service.
requirements.source_quote: The category is set by whoever logged the complaint. If it's wrong you can change it here, but you have to put a note in saying why.

requirements.statement: When the handler changes the category of a complaint, the system requires a note that says why the category was changed.
requirements.rationale: The expert states the rule; whether the system enforces it or it is a team practice is an open question.
requirements.source_quote: If it's wrong you can change it here, but you have to put a note in saying why.

requirements.statement: The system sends a standard acknowledgement letter within 4 working days of receiving a complaint.
requirements.rationale: Seen only on the timeline: "Acknowledgement sent — Standard acknowledgement letter, 4 working days". The expert did not describe acknowledgement; whether the system or a person sends it is an open question.
requirements.source_quote: on the right is the timeline, every event in order: received, acknowledged, assigned, and so on.

requirements.statement: When a complaint is logged, the system assigns it to a handler from the queue for its category.
requirements.rationale: Seen only on the timeline: "Assigned to Vibo Walridge — Auto-assigned from the Delayed claim queue". The expert did not describe assignment, and the frame shows Owner as Mabo Grawell, so the relationship between Owner and Assigned to is an open question.
requirements.source_quote: on the right is the timeline, every event in order: received, acknowledged, assigned, and so on.

requirements.statement: The system requires the handler to select exactly one Outcome from Uphold, Partially uphold and Reject before it records a decision.
requirements.rationale: Outcome is a radio group marked with an asterisk. Help text seen: Uphold "The complaint is justified in full. Redress is usually due."; Partially uphold "Part of the complaint is justified. Redress may be due."; Reject "The complaint is not justified. No redress."
requirements.source_quote: It's three options: uphold, partially uphold, or reject. You pick one, choose a reason from the dropdown, and write the summary in the box.

requirements.statement: The system requires the handler to choose a Reason from the Reason dropdown before it records a decision.
requirements.rationale: Reason is marked with a red asterisk. Only one value, "Delay not fully explained", was visible; the full list is an open question.
requirements.source_quote: You pick one, choose a reason from the dropdown, and write the summary in the box.

requirements.statement: The system requires the Summary of findings to contain at least 50 words before it records a decision.
requirements.rationale: Counter under the box on the frame reads "At least 50 words. Currently 31 words." How a word is counted is an open question.
requirements.source_quote: The summary is mandatory and it has to be at least fifty words, the system counts them.

requirements.statement: The Decision screen shows the current word count of the Summary of findings as the handler types.
requirements.rationale: Seen on the frame: "At least 50 words. Currently 31 words."
requirements.source_quote: The summary is mandatory and it has to be at least fifty words, the system counts them.

requirements.statement: When the handler presses Record decision, the system stores the Outcome, Reason and Summary of findings as the decision on the complaint.
requirements.rationale: The recorded decision is what unlocks the Send letter button and feeds the letter and the uphold rate.
requirements.source_quote: Then you press Record decision.

requirements.statement: The system allows only complaint handlers at grade 2 or above to record a decision.
requirements.rationale: Banner on the frame: "Grade 2 and above. Only complaint handlers at grade 2 or above can record a decision. Trainees: ask your supervisor to record it." A trainee's supervisor records the decision for them.
requirements.source_quote: Only complaint handlers at grade two and above can record a decision. If you're a trainee the button is greyed out and your supervisor records it for you.

requirements.statement: When a handler below grade 2 views the Decision screen, the system shows the Record decision button disabled.
requirements.source_quote: If you're a trainee the button is greyed out and your supervisor records it for you.

requirements.statement: The handler can save the Decision screen as a draft without recording the decision.
requirements.rationale: Seen only as a Save draft button next to Record decision; the expert did not mention drafts. What a draft saves and who sees it is an open question.
requirements.source_quote: Then you press Record decision.

requirements.statement: For a complaint with an Outcome of Uphold or Partially uphold, the handler records redress on the Redress screen.
requirements.rationale: The path for a Reject outcome, and for a partial uphold with no money owed, was not shown.
requirements.source_quote: If it's upheld or partially upheld, you go to Redress.

requirements.statement: The Redress screen requires a Refund amount in pounds before it calculates redress.
requirements.rationale: Both fields are marked with a red asterisk. Values seen: 750.00 and 90.
requirements.source_quote: You put in the refund amount and the number of days the customer was out of pocket, and it works out the interest and the total in the little table.

requirements.statement: The Redress screen requires a Days out of pocket count before it calculates redress.
requirements.rationale: Both fields are marked with a red asterisk. Values seen: 750.00 and 90.
requirements.source_quote: You put in the refund amount and the number of days the customer was out of pocket, and it works out the interest and the total in the little table.

requirements.statement: The system calculates the interest and the Total redress from the Refund amount and the Days out of pocket and shows them in the Calculation table.
requirements.rationale: Calculation table rows seen: Refund £750.00; Interest (8% for 90 days) £14.79; Total redress £764.79. The handler presses Recalculate to fill the table.
requirements.source_quote: You put in the refund amount and the number of days the customer was out of pocket, and it works out the interest and the total in the little table.

requirements.statement: The system takes the interest rate for redress from the Finance rate table and shows it on the Redress screen as read-only.
requirements.rationale: Field on the frame: Interest rate "8.00% per year", greyed out, help text "From the Finance rate table. Not editable here." Where the table lives is an open question.
requirements.source_quote: The interest rate comes from somewhere in finance, I just use whatever it shows.

requirements.statement: The system calculates interest as simple interest: Refund amount × annual interest rate × Days out of pocket ÷ 365, rounded to the nearest penny.
requirements.rationale: Banner on the frame: "Interest is simple interest at the Finance rate table figure, calculated from the number of days the customer was out of pocket." The figures seen (750.00 × 8% × 90 ÷ 365 = 14.79) fit a 365-day year; rounding and leap years were not stated.
requirements.source_quote: it works out the interest and the total in the little table.

requirements.statement: The system shows Total redress as the Refund amount plus the calculated interest.
requirements.rationale: Bold total row on the frame: £764.79 = £750.00 + £14.79.
requirements.source_quote: it works out the interest and the total in the little table.

requirements.statement: When the handler presses Approve redress, the system records the Total redress as approved on the complaint.
requirements.source_quote: Then you press Approve redress.

requirements.statement: When the redress is more than £500, the system requires a second approval from the team lead before the redress is approved.
requirements.rationale: On the frame: "Redress over £500 needs a second approver (team lead)." Whether the threshold applies to the total or the refund, and what happens while approval is pending, are open questions.
requirements.source_quote: Anything over five hundred pounds needs a second approver, and that pops up as a task for the team lead.

requirements.statement: When redress needs a second approval, the system creates a task for the team lead to approve it.
requirements.source_quote: Anything over five hundred pounds needs a second approver, and that pops up as a task for the team lead.

requirements.statement: The system builds the final response letter from a template by merging in the customer's name and address, the complaint reference, policy, product, received date, decision, summary of findings, redress amounts and handler name from the complaint, decision and redress records.
requirements.rationale: Merge fields seen on the frame: letter date, customer name and address (first name repeated in 'Dear Vinel,'), Our reference, policy, product, received date, decision, summary of findings, total redress with refund and interest, and handler name in the sign-off.
requirements.source_quote: It's a template with the customer's name, the reference, the decision and the redress amount merged in from the earlier screens.

requirements.statement: The Letter Preview highlights every merged field in the letter.
requirements.rationale: Seen on the frame: banner "Merge fields are highlighted" and highlighted values in the letter. The expert did not mention the highlighting.
requirements.source_quote: It's a template with the customer's name, the reference, the decision and the redress amount merged in from the earlier screens.

requirements.statement: The system shows the Send letter button on Letter Preview only after a decision has been recorded on the complaint.
requirements.rationale: On the frame: "Send letter appears only once a decision is recorded." Whether a saved draft counts as recorded is an open question.
requirements.source_quote: You can't send a letter until a decision is recorded, the Send letter button just won't show up.

requirements.statement: When the handler presses Send letter, the system sends the final response letter to print.
requirements.rationale: What "print" means (print queue, mailing house, PDF) is an open question.
requirements.source_quote: You read it through, and if it's right you press Send letter and it goes to print.

requirements.statement: When the customer has asked for email, the system sends the final response letter by email instead of print.
requirements.rationale: Banner on the frame: "The letter is sent by post unless the customer asked for email." The expert does not know where the preference is held.
requirements.source_quote: If the customer asked for email, it's supposed to email it instead of printing. I'm not sure where that preference is set, it's not on any of these screens.

requirements.statement: The Dashboard shows three figures for the team: the number of open complaints, the number breaching the 8-week SLA, and the uphold rate.
requirements.rationale: Tiles seen: Open complaints 34 "across the team today"; Breaching SLA 4 "past the 8-week deadline", in red; Uphold rate 38% "upheld or partially upheld".
requirements.source_quote: Three numbers: open complaints, how many are breaching SLA, and the uphold rate, and a chart of complaints received by month.

requirements.statement: The Dashboard shows a bar chart of the number of complaints received in each month.
requirements.rationale: Six months were shown on the frame (Apr 2026 to Sep 2026); how many months to show was not stated.
requirements.source_quote: a chart of complaints received by month.

requirements.statement: The Dashboard calculates the uphold rate as the percentage of decided complaints whose Outcome is Uphold or Partially uphold.
requirements.rationale: Tile caption on the frame: "upheld or partially upheld". The period the rate covers is an open question.
requirements.source_quote: I think the uphold rate is this month, but it might be rolling, I've never checked.

requirements.statement: When the team lead presses Export on the Dashboard, the system produces a spreadsheet file of the dashboard figures.
requirements.rationale: On the frame: "Exports the figures above as a spreadsheet." The file layout is an open question.
requirements.source_quote: You press Export to get it all as a spreadsheet.

questions.question: How exactly is SLA remaining calculated: from which date and time does the clock start, does it count calendar or working days, when is the 8-week end point, and what is known about the cases where the clock is wrong? Is the automatic Ombudsman referral driven by the same clock?
questions.why_it_matters: The SLA drives the inbox sort order, the Breached flag, the automatic Ombudsman referral and the Breaching SLA dashboard figure; the expert says the current clock is sometimes wrong, so the rule must be pinned down rather than copied.
questions.context_quote: Sometimes the SLA clock is wrong, honestly, nobody knows why, so you double-check the received date.

questions.question: What does the automatic Ombudsman referral do beyond changing the status to Referred: is anything sent to the Ombudsman or the customer, who is notified, and can a handler still work the complaint afterwards?
questions.why_it_matters: The delivery team needs to know whether this is a status change or an integration with an external body, and what happens to the complaint after it.
questions.context_quote: Anything over eight weeks old goes to the Ombudsman automatically, you'll see the status flip to Referred on its own.

questions.question: Does the Complaints Inbox show every open complaint in the system or only the handler's team? What defines the team, why does the list include a row with Owner 'Unassigned', and can a handler see other teams' complaints?
questions.why_it_matters: The inbox is the first thing a handler sees; the visibility rule decides who can see and pick up which complaints.
questions.context_quote: You land on the Inbox, which is every open complaint sorted by how long we've got left on it.

questions.question: What is the full list of statuses (New, Investigating, Awaiting customer, Decided and Referred were seen), what does "open" mean for the inbox and the dashboard, and what moves a complaint from one status to the next: a handler by hand, or the system when a decision is recorded or a letter is sent?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert never described how status changes; without the transitions the workflow cannot be built and the Open complaints figure cannot be defined.
questions.context_quote: Each row has the reference, the customer, when it came in, the category, the status and the SLA countdown.

questions.question: How do Owner and "Assigned to" relate? On the frame the Owner is Mabo Grawell but the timeline says the complaint was auto-assigned to Vibo Walridge. How does auto-assignment from a category queue work, and can a complaint be reassigned by hand?
questions.why_it_matters: Ownership decides whose inbox the complaint appears in and who is responsible for the deadline.
questions.context_quote: on the right is the timeline, every event in order: received, acknowledged, assigned, and so on.

questions.question: Is the note explaining a category change enforced by the system (for example a mandatory reason box when pressing Change), or is it a team rule the handler is expected to follow?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether the delivery team must build a validation or only document a process.
questions.context_quote: If it's wrong you can change it here, but you have to put a note in saying why.

questions.question: Does "notes cannot be edited or deleted" apply to every user, including supervisors and administrators, and is there any way to correct a note entered by mistake (for example by adding a correcting note)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets the permissions model for the audit trail and what to do about genuine mistakes.
questions.context_quote: Notes can't be edited or deleted once they're saved.

questions.question: Is the acknowledgement letter sent by the system within 4 working days of receipt, or by a person, and what template and channel does it use?
questions.why_it_matters: The timeline shows an acknowledgement event but the expert did not cover it; if it is automatic it is a scheduled job the delivery team must build.
questions.context_quote: on the right is the timeline, every event in order: received, acknowledged, assigned, and so on.

questions.question: What are all the options in the Reason dropdown, and do they depend on the Outcome or the category chosen?
questions.why_it_matters: Only one value ("Delay not fully explained") was visible; the list is reference data the delivery team must load.
questions.context_quote: You pick one, choose a reason from the dropdown, and write the summary in the box.

questions.question: How are words counted for the 50-word minimum (numbers, hyphenated words, references like CMP-2026-01518), and is there a maximum length for the summary?
questions.why_it_matters: The count decides whether Record decision is allowed, so the counting rule must be exact.
questions.context_quote: The summary is mandatory and it has to be at least fifty words, the system counts them.

questions.question: How does the system know a handler's grade (a role, a user attribute, an HR feed)? When a supervisor records a decision for a trainee, is it recorded under the supervisor's name or the trainee's, and can a decision be changed after it is recorded?
questions.why_it_matters: Needed to build the permission check and to attribute decisions correctly for audit and the uphold-rate figure.
questions.context_quote: If you're a trainee the button is greyed out and your supervisor records it for you.

questions.question: What does Save draft save, who can see a draft decision, and does a draft count as "a decision is recorded" for the purpose of showing the Send letter button?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert did not mention drafts; the delivery team needs the draft lifecycle and confirmation that a draft must not unlock the letter.
questions.context_quote: Then you press Record decision.

questions.question: Where does the Finance rate table live and how does the system read it: a table in this system or a feed from a finance system? Which rate applies when the rate changes: the rate on the day of calculation, or the rate over the period out of pocket?
questions.why_it_matters: The interest figure goes into the customer's letter and payment, so the source and versioning of the rate must be defined.
questions.context_quote: The interest rate comes from somewhere in finance, I just use whatever it shows.

questions.question: What is the exact interest formula: day-count basis (365 or 366 days in a leap year), rounding rule, and is interest applied to the refund amount only?
questions.why_it_matters: The figures on screen (750.00 at 8% for 90 days = £14.79) fit 365-day simple interest, but rounding and leap-year handling were not stated and affect what the customer is paid.
questions.context_quote: it works out the interest and the total in the little table.

questions.question: When redress over £500 needs a second approver, what happens next: does the complaint wait until the team lead approves, can the letter be sent before that, who counts as the team lead, and what happens if the team lead rejects or changes the amount? Is the £500 threshold on the Total redress or the refund only?
questions.why_it_matters: This is a control on paying money out; the delivery team needs the full approval workflow, not just the trigger.
questions.context_quote: Anything over five hundred pounds needs a second approver, and that pops up as a task for the team lead.

questions.question: For a rejected complaint, or a partially upheld complaint with no money owed, is the Redress screen skipped, and does the letter template change to leave out the payment paragraph?
questions.why_it_matters: The walkthrough only showed the partially upheld path with a payment; the other outcomes need their own path through redress and the letter.
questions.context_quote: If it's upheld or partially upheld, you go to Redress.

questions.question: Where is the customer's preference for email over post held, and how does the system read it when Send letter is pressed?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert says email is supposed to happen instead of print but the preference is not on any screen shown, so the source of that data is unknown.
questions.context_quote: If the customer asked for email, it's supposed to email it instead of printing. I'm not sure where that preference is set, it's not on any of these screens.

questions.question: What does "goes to print" mean technically (a print queue, a mailing house, a PDF)? Is a copy of the sent letter stored on the complaint, and does sending the letter change the complaint status or close it?
questions.why_it_matters: Sending the final response is the end of the process; the delivery team needs the integration and the record it leaves.
questions.context_quote: You read it through, and if it's right you press Send letter and it goes to print.

questions.question: Who is allowed to use Edit template, and does it change the template for every future letter or only the letter for this complaint? Are the fixed sentences (payment within 10 working days, Ombudsman referral within six months) regulatory wording that must stay uneditable?
questions.why_it_matters: Editing a template used for regulated final responses needs clear ownership and controls; the Edit template button was seen but never described.
questions.context_quote: It's a template with the customer's name, the reference, the decision and the redress amount merged in from the earlier screens.

questions.question: Over what period is the uphold rate calculated (this calendar month, a rolling window, or all time), and is it based on decisions recorded or complaints received in that period?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert is unsure; the figure is a headline team-performance measure and its definition must be agreed before it is built.
questions.context_quote: I think the uphold rate is this month, but it might be rolling, I've never checked.

questions.question: Who can see the Dashboard, and how is the team it shows chosen? The frame shows a grade 2 handler viewing 'Team view for Dalo Walwell's team' although the expert says it is for the team lead.
questions.why_it_matters: Decides access control for the dashboard and whether a handler can see teams other than their own.
questions.context_quote: And the Dashboard is what the team lead looks at.

questions.question: What exactly does Export contain and in what format: the three headline figures, the monthly counts, or the underlying complaint list, and how many months of history?
questions.why_it_matters: The screen only says "Exports the figures above as a spreadsheet"; the delivery team needs the file layout.
questions.context_quote: You press Export to get it all as a spreadsheet.

questions.question: What are the Reports and Settings pages in the left navigation, and how is a complaint first logged? The walkthrough starts with complaints already in the inbox.
questions.why_it_matters: Two navigation items and the logging step were never shown, so the scope of the system is bigger than the walkthrough covers.
questions.context_quote: That's the whole process, inbox to letter.
